home.section.painpoints.title: Do you recognize these friction points in your operations?
home.section.painpoints.desc: The operational bottlenecks SMEs and mid-market companies face most often, and the answer I propose for each.
painpoint.p1.problem: Your teams re-enter the same information across multiple disconnected tools.
painpoint.p1.solution: Automation and synchronisation between your tools, using n8n flows (automation software) and APIs (interfaces that connect software).
painpoint.p2.problem: Your data is available but difficult to interpret and actionable too late.
painpoint.p2.solution: A business intelligence platform (data-driven steering) with metrics defined once and dashboards for leadership.
painpoint.p2.impact: Readable metrics at the right time
painpoint.p3.problem: Your operational workflows depend on untracked, manual email-based approvals.
painpoint.p3.solution: AI agents with human approval steps and a complete audit log of every decision.
painpoint.p4.problem: Your tools don't talk to each other and every new use requires custom development.
painpoint.p4.solution: Documented connections between your software (APIs, n8n) and a shared database, set up one workflow at a time.
painpoint.p4.impact: Connected tools, without a full rebuild
painpoint.p5.problem: Employees spend excessive time searching, verifying, and transferring fragmented knowledge.
painpoint.p5.solution: An AI assistant that searches your internal documents and cites its sources (RAG: answers grounded in document retrieval).
painpoint.p5.impact: Sourced answers, from your own documents

home.faq.q1: How long does it take to deliver an enterprise AI project?
home.faq.a1: It depends on the scope: a prototype (POC, proof of concept) usually takes 4 to 6 weeks, a full go-live a few months. I deploy in stages so each one delivers measurable value.
home.faq.q2: How do you protect the security and confidentiality of our data?
home.faq.a2: I sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) before any exchange of sensitive information. Your data stays in an environment chosen with you (European Union or your own servers) and is not used to train models.
home.faq.q3: What types of enterprises do you partner with?
home.faq.a3: Leaders of SMEs and mid-market companies, and their CIOs, who have tested AI and want real, reliable and compliant use. I adapt systems to your digital maturity, without forcing a disruptive overhaul.
home.faq.q4: Do you provide end-to-end digital transformation consulting?
home.faq.a4: Yes, within my scope: maturity audit, process automation, data-driven steering and AI governance. For topics outside that scope, I point you to the right people.
home.faq.q5: What happens during an initial discovery call?
home.faq.a5: A free 20-minute call to understand your challenges. If the need is confirmed, I send you a written proposal within 5 business days. No commitment.

home.run.s1.question: Which customers are at risk of not renewing this quarter?
home.run.s1.answer: Three accounts show two signals at once: orders down for two months [2] and a ticket unresolved for more than three weeks [3]. For two of them, the last sales contact was more than 60 days ago [1].
home.run.s1.action: Draft a personalised follow-up email for each of the three accounts, to be sent by the account owner.
home.run.s1.decision: The « Renewal risk » dashboard is updated and each account owner receives an alert.
home.run.s2.question: Which orders are at risk of late delivery?
home.run.s2.answer: Two orders depend on an item out of stock at the supplier [2]; a third has been stuck in transit for four days [3]. All three have a promised date less than ten days away [1].
home.run.s2.action: Offer the three customers a revised delivery date, with a message prepared for customer service.
home.run.s2.decision: The « Orders at risk » indicator on the logistics dashboard is updated, with the reason for each delay.
home.run.s3.question: What does the supplier contract say about late delivery?
home.run.s3.answer: Article 9 of the contract sets a penalty per week of delay, with a cap [1]. The amendment signed later raises that cap [2]. The supplier confirmed these terms in writing [3].
home.run.s3.action: Create an alert before each of this supplier's delivery deadlines, with a reminder of the applicable penalties.
home.run.s3.decision: Contract deadlines appear on the purchasing dashboard, each linked to the clause it comes from.
